coordinate_conversion: Blender (x,y,z) -> Godot (x,z,-y); model faces +Z, player rotates model by PI to face -Z.

Grab.sampling: Seek by validated grab progress; hold contact at end.

Pickup.sampling: Ownership confirmed: contact-to-carry lift; about2x playback can keep the game responsive.

Carry.sampling: Static held-object pose; stable two-palm object socket.

RunCarry.source: Run plus carried-arm targets relative to running chest

Aim.sampling: 37 samples over source frames1-38: windup ends on the same hand contact as Throw release. Hold ready pose; charge timer remains independent.

Throw.sampling: Starts on the authored release pose. Physics release remains immediate on validated input; never play for non-launch drops.

Tug_Fast.source: Tug_Elder_Woman_Fast for Elder/Woman, existing Young_Elder retimed for Young

Tug_Slow.source: Tug_Elder_Woman_Slow for Elder/Woman, existing Young_Elder retimed for Young

notes: Original bone proportions/meshes/weights retained; all world-space grip constraints are evaluated before controllers are removed.

The baked GLB reparents neck and both clavicles to root at unchanged rest coordinates. This represents Blender scale-isolated branches in glTF without shearing/shortening the arms during chest breathing. The source editable rig hierarchy is unchanged.
Young keeps his existing authored tug; no new Young dance or redesign.
Tug clips are actor-local baked poses: shared object travel and authored stage spacing are metadata, not extra mesh geometry.
No overhead two-hand throw is exported. No animation may change ownership, launch velocity, score or authority.

godot_import.reason: Keep constant reset keys so every clip clears prior chest scale and hair offsets.
